data.text: The invention relates to an apparatus for manufacturing green bricks from clay for the brick manufacturing industry. The apparatus comprises a circulating conveyor carrying mould containers combined to mould container parts. The apparatus comprises a reservoir for clay arranged above the mould containers. The apparatus comprises means for carrying clay out of the reservoir into the mould containers. The apparatus comprises means for pressing and trimming clay in the mould containers. The apparatus comprises means for supplying and placing take-off plates for the green bricks. The apparatus comprises means for discharging green bricks released from the mould containers. Such an apparatus is known in the field. The apparatus is for instance described in the patent 1000186 of applicant. The known apparatus is suitable for automated production. The known apparatus is suitable for large numbers of green bricks. The known apparatus is for the brick manufacturing industry. The bricks fired from these green bricks have a substantially smooth appearance. The bricks fired from these green bricks have a uniform appearance. A recent demand has developed on the market for bricks. The bricks appear as if they have been manufactured according to traditional methods. The invention has for its object to adapt the known apparatus. The invention has for its object such that it can produce in automated manner large numbers of green bricks with a traditional appearance. [0004]     The apparatus according to the invention has the feature that the apparatus further comprises means for moving the mould container parts filled with green bricks. The apparatus further comprises means for moving the mould container parts filled with green bricks such that a protruding edge is formed on at least one side of the green bricks. The bricks fired from the green bricks produced using the apparatus according to the invention impart beautiful shadow effects to the wall into which they have been built. The shadow effects appear when the sun shines thereon. This aesthetic effect is an important commercial advantage. The edge-forming means are preferably adapted to move the mould container parts. The edge-forming means are adapted to move the mould container parts repeatedly for a certain period. Repetition a number of times is found in practice to be sufficient to obtain the intended effect. Repetition, for instance three times, is found in practice to be sufficient to obtain the intended effect. In a practical preferred embodiment the edge-forming means are adapted to move the mould container parts. The edge-forming means are adapted to move the mould container parts substantially transversely of the transporting direction. In a further preferred embodiment, the edge-forming means comprise a frame. The frame is adapted to engage individually on a mould container part. This preferred embodiment has the significant advantage. The edge-forming means can act on one mould container part. Another mould container part undergoes another operation. The another mould container part is for instance filled with clay. The edge-forming means can therefore be added to the known apparatus. This does not affect the production time. In yet another preferred embodiment the frame spans the mould container part. The frame is provided on both sides with stop members. The stop members are situated during operation at the location of the side walls of the mould container part. An exceptionally compact embodiment of the invention is hereby realized. The embodiment utilizes the available space economically. The embodiment can be arranged without difficulty on the known apparatus. In order to prevent unnecessary damage to the mould container parts, these latter are provided on their side walls with stop surfaces. The stop surfaces are preferably of plastic. In preference, the stop members of the frame of the edge-forming means are also provided with these stop surfaces. The stop surfaces are preferably plastic. The invention is described in more detail hereinbelow with reference to the drawing. Figure 1 shows schematically a preferred embodiment of the apparatus according to the invention. Figure 2 shows in more detail a perspective view of a part of the apparatus of figure 1 with the edge-forming means therein. Figure 3 shows the edge-forming means of figure 2 in even more detail. Figure 4 is a perspective view of a first preferred embodiment of a mould container part which is suitable for use in the apparatus according to the invention. Figure 5 is a perspective view of a second preferred embodiment of a mould container part. Figure 6 shows schematically a part of a wall which has been built using bricks provided with an edge and fired from the green bricks manufactured using the apparatus according to the invention. Like components are provided in the figures with like reference numerals. Figure 1 shows a preferred embodiment of an apparatus. The apparatus is for manufacturing green bricks. The apparatus is for the brick manufacturing industry according to the invention. Apparatus 1 comprises a conveyor 3. Mould containers combined to a unit are placed on the conveyor. The mould containers are placed in the form of a mould container part 4 on the conveyor. The mould container parts fit closely against each other. Placed above the mould containers is a reservoir 5 for clay. The reservoir 5 for clay is kept in continuous movement by an agitator 6. The agitator 6 is driven by the electric motor 7. Clay is supplied to reservoir 5. Clay is supplied by a circulating conveyor 8. The clay is carried out of reservoir 5 into the mould containers. The clay is then pressed down by pressing device 9. Pressing device 9 is pivotable on shaft 10. The excess clay is also trimmed using means which are not drawn. The device 11 carries take-off plates 12. The device carries take-off plates 12 onto a mould container part. After turning over of the mould container part, the green bricks 13 come to lie on the plates. The green bricks 13 come to lie on the plates after being released from the mould containers. Edge-forming means 22 are arranged between device 9 and device 11. The edge-forming means move each mould container part 4. The edge-forming means move each mould container part 4 such that a protruding edge forms on the upper side of the green bricks received therein. Figure 2 shows in more detail the part of apparatus 1. The part of apparatus 1 comprises edge-forming means 22. In the shown preferred embodiment, the edge-forming means 22 comprise a frame 26. The frame 26 spans mould container part 4. Frame 26 is provided on either side with stop members 27. The stop members 27 are situated at the position of side walls 30 of the mould container part. The distance between stop members 27 is greater than the length of the mould container part. Frame 26 can be moved reciprocally by means of drive 31. Drive 31 is designated by means of arrow B. In preference the direction of movement B of frame 26 lies substantially transversely of the transporting direction T of conveyor 3. By moving frame 26 repeatedly, the stop members 27 strike alternately against the side walls 30 of the mould container part 4. The mould container part 4 is spanned at that moment by frame 26. As a result the relevant mould container part is shaken back and forth. The green bricks 13 situated during operation in mould containers 21 rise a certain distance in the mould containers. The green bricks 13 are situated during operation in mould containers 21 of mould container part 4. This results in the intended edge forming on the upper side of each green brick. Drive 31 is preferably an eccentric drive. Drive 31 can subject heavy components to a smooth movement. Drive 31 can subject heavy components to a smooth movement owing to a good distribution of forces. The eccentric drive can for instance be adjusted such that the moment a stop member comes up against one of the side walls of a mould container part. The maximum force is exerted by the drive on this mould container part. Each mould container part 4 is coupled with some clearance to conveyor 3. Each mould container part 4 is coupled in the direction of movement B. In the shown preferred embodiment each mould container part is even disengageably coupled to an associated chain part 15. The chain part 15 is of chain conveyor 3. The coupling of both parts takes place using the bolt-nut connections 16. The coupling of both parts takes place using the bolt-nut connections 17. Bolt holes 33 are given an oval form. Bolt holes 33 are given an oval form in order to create the necessary clearance. Chain part 15 of chain conveyor 3 comprises ears 18, 19, and 20. Ears 18, 19, and 20 serve as links of the chain conveyor. It is noted that instead of a chain conveyor many other conveyors known in the field can be used. Figure 3 shows edge-forming means 22. Figure 3 shows edge-forming means 22 in more detail. So as to prevent damage, stop members 27 are provided with stop surfaces 28. Corresponding stop surfaces 29 are arranged on side walls 30 of the mould container parts. The stop surfaces are preferably of plastic. Each mould container part 4 is further provided at both sides with spacer members 32 on walls 30. These spacer members protrude slightly above the mould container part itself. These spacer members protrude so that take-off plates 12 can rest thereon. The take-off plates 12 can rest thereon without damaging the edge. The edge has just been formed on green bricks 13. It has been found in practice that the form of green bricks 13, including the edge, is retained after the mould container part has been turned over. Figure 4 shows a first preferred embodiment of a mould container part 4 and a chain part 15 in an uncoupled situation. The different mould containers 21 are combined to a unit. The unit is on mould container part 4. It is noted that the use of edge-forming means 22 has the further important advantage. The advantage is that additional means for releasing the green bricks from the mould containers are no longer necessary. An example of such releasing means known in the field are bottoms 23. The bottoms 23 are displaceable by means of ejectors 24. The ejectors 24 are such as are arranged in the second preferred embodiment shown in figure 5. This ejector lies under bias of spring 25. Spring 25 centres the ejector. The ejector is such that no separate guiding is necessary in chain part 15. Ejector 24 is operated by a per se known driving device (not shown) during release of the green bricks. These releasing means are used by applicant. These releasing means are used in a number of their apparatuses. These releasing means are the subject of the patent 1000186 in the name of applicant. Figure 5 shows how the mould container parts and chain parts of the known apparatus can be used in combination with the edge-forming means according to the invention. Figure 5 shows how with some modifications the mould container parts of the known apparatus can be used in combination with the edge-forming means according to the invention. Figure 5 shows how with some modifications the chain parts of the known apparatus can be used in combination with the edge-forming means according to the invention. The modifications relate to enlargement of the holes 34 for ejectors 24. The modifications relate to enlargement of the holes 34 such that mould container part 4 is coupled to chain part 15 with some clearance in the direction of movement B. Holes 34 can for instance be oval for this purpose. It is noted that the multi-part mould container part as described in applicant's non-prepublished patent application 1007600 can also be made suitable in like manner for use in an apparatus. The apparatus is provided with the edge-forming means according to the invention. Figure 6 shows a wall 35. The wall 35 is built from bricks 36. The bricks 36 are provided with a protruding edge 37. The apparatus according to the invention is used. It is possible to imagine that an exceptional shadow effect can be caused by sunlight. The sunlight is incident upon the wall. Field of the Invention. Sentence one. Sentence two. The present invention relates to a display device. The display device is for appreciation regarding pseudo space such as in the water or in the air. The display device is for appreciation regarding creatures and/or objects which float in the air. The creatures and/or objects are represented by fish, submarines, spaceships, airships, butterflies, birds, and the like. Background Art. Recently, for a purpose of refreshing feelings of residents and the like indoors, interiors with motifs in the water or in the air are provided at homes. Recently, interiors with motifs in the water or in the air are provided in the offices. As such interiors, examples of interiors with motifs in the water include aquariums. The examples include aquariums in which seaweeds or tropical fish are put. The aquariums are in a simple water tank. Recently, aquariums are used not only at home but also at shops and the like. Aquariums are used as a display for visual effects. Aquariums keep aquatic animals such as tropical fish and the like. Aquariums keep aquatic plants such as seaweeds and the like. The aquatic animals and plants are kept in a water tank. In order to keep aquatic animals such as tropical fish and the like which are real creatures, living conditions inherent to the creatures including foods, water temperature, and the like should be maintained. This should accompany labor cost. This should accompany maintenance cost. In order to reduce such labor, a display device is proposed. The display device is proposed in Japan unexamined patent publication Hei7-230259. The display device is provided with pseudo models of aquatic animals such as fish models and the like. The display device is provided by generating the air bubble from a ventilation member which is installed at the bottom wall of a water tank. The display device generates water flow in a water tank and makes viewers feel as if pseudo models of aquatic animals such as fish models are swimming as a pseudo aquarium. The display device is a pseudo aquarium in which daily feeding is not required. Environmental maintenance such as temperature maintenance and the like are easy in the pseudo aquarium. However, since the above display device generates water flow in a water tank by directly generating air bubble in the water tank in which pseudo creature models are floating, creature models get an imbalance. Since creature models get an imbalance and behave unnaturally since air bubble adheres to the creature models. In addition, in peripheral domains where air bubble near the air bubble generating member rises. When the creature models go in said domains, the aquatic animal pseudo models are pushed upward near the water surface by air bubble. They show unnatural behavior. They show unnatural behavior, lying down. The same is applied when pseudo creature models are replaced by models. The models are such as submarines. The models are other than fish. In addition, when this water tank for appreciation is made to be a display which expresses a space other than underwater space, for example, cosmic space where spaceships and the like exist, or a space with a motif where birds and butterflies and the like exist. Since rising air bubble exists around spaceships, birds, butterflies, and the like, this water tank for appreciation is not suitable for a display which expresses a space other than underwater space. The object of the present invention is to provide a water tank for appreciation. The water tank does not cause imbalance of models by air bubble adhesion. The water tank does not cause sudden rising of models in the vicinity of air bubble generating member. The water tank does not cause lying down in the vicinity of a water surface. The models such as creature models represented by fish models, for example, naturally swimming show more natural movement and behavior in the water tank. This invention relates to a stuffing/dosing machine. The stuffing/dosing machine comprises a tilting hopper. The tilting hopper is suitable for forming and optionally dosing flowable food materials. The flowable food materials include whole meat joints, meat cut into pieces or minced, meat masses, cheeses, fine pastas and jams, inter alia. The flowable food materials particularly include meat cut into pieces or minced. The stuffing/dosing machine is compact. The stuffing/dosing machine has high adherence properties. The stuffing/dosing machine is for example meat masses for making mortadellas and salamis. The stuffing/dosing machine is for meat at a relatively low temperature. The meat is at a temperature between 0°C and -5°C. The text provides background to the invention. Patent WO 99/29178, in the name of the current applicant, describes a stuffing/dosing machine of this type. The stuffing/dosing machine comprises a hopper like deposit containing a food material. The hopper like deposit can be closed hermetically. A vacuum has been created in the hopper like deposit. The stuffing/dosing machine comprises two stuffing cylinders, which operate alternatively. The stuffing cylinders are provided with corresponding pistons that perform a first section of their respective strokes directly within a narrowed area or antechamber in the lower part of the deposit in order to stir and push the food material as far as respective stuffing-dosing chambers. The stuffing-dosing chambers are placed at the base of said deposit and aligned coaxially with the cylinders. The pistons perform a second section within said stuffing-dosing chambers to compact and introduce the food material into respective collector pipes. The collector pipes are connected to a rotary collector/distributor valve. The movement of the rotary collector/distributor valve is synchronised with that of said stuffing cylinders to give way alternatively to the food material driven by one or other of the cylinders towards a common outlet duct. The speed and travel of the cylinder strokes and the movements of the valve are controlled by regulating means. The regulating means provides a single continuous flow of food materials in said outlet conduit. Optionally, the regulating means provides an interrupted flow of precisely dosed portions. The said two stuffing cylinders are located outside the deposit. The said two stuffing cylinders are located parallel to one another and in proximity. The said two stuffing cylinders are in a slightly inclined position. The said two stuffing cylinders are housed in an empty section of a side wall of the deposit. Their corresponding stems extend through the deposit wall. Their corresponding stems extend to actuate in the antechamber. Their corresponding stems extend to actuate in the stuffing-dosing chambers located at the base of the deposit. In this way, the deposit, the antechamber, the cylinders, the pistons and the stuffing-dosing chambers form an ensemble or first structural unit. The first structural unit is articulated at the base thereof with respect to the machine bed. The first structural unit can tilt. The first structural unit moves between a first position, or operative position. In the first position, lower mouthpieces of the stuffing-dosing chambers are hermetically positioned in higher inlet mouthpieces of said alternative valve. The first structural unit moves between a second position, or cleaning and maintenance position. In the second position, lower mouthpieces of the stuffing-dosing chambers are separated from said higher inlet mouthpieces of the alternative valve to a sufficient degree to enable easy access to both mouthpieces. The present invention relates to footwear. More particularly, the present invention relates to a footwear construction. The present invention relates to a method for making the footwear construction. Such footwear is targeted toward individuals who must occasionally traverse wet or damp areas or worksites. Conventional footwear constructions provide one of durability, comfort, or waterproofing. Conventional footwear constructions usually do not provide all three because the features required for these characteristics typically negate one another. For example, one construction known for its durability is a direct attach construction. The direct attach construction may be incorporated into work or hiking boots. In such a construction, a midsole is present. The midsole is constructed of a soft, resilient material. The midsole provides a uniform-depth cushion along the entire length of the shoe. The cushion is between the upper and the more rigid and durable outsole. This midsole is constructed with a process. The midsole is direct attached to the upper from heel to toe in a mold. BACKGROUND. Field. The invention relates generally to the field of displays for portable handheld electronic devices. The invention relates more particularly to a display. The display is switched between portrait and landscape modes. The switching is as a function of a sensed orientation of the user. Background. Portable data and media display devices, such as mobile telephones, e-book readers, tablet computers and the like typically have rectangular display screens. Portable data and media display devices typically have a "portrait" orientation. It is often desirable to view content in a "landscape" orientation. This can be accomplished by rotating the display screen by 90°. This can be accomplished by selecting a landscape presentation. This can be accomplished by selecting a landscape display mode. A manual selection may be provided. Many devices now have inertial sensors to automatically select a landscape presentation. The inertial sensors automatically select a landscape presentation when rotation of the device is sensed. In some situations, the user of a portable device may not want the display mode to change when the device is rotated. For example, a user may start reading email messages while sitting upright. For example, a user may start playing a game while sitting upright. The user may then decide to lie down while continuing to use the device. The user does not want the display mode to change in such a situation. The relative orientation of the user's eyes with respect to the display screen has not changed. While a manual display mode selection may be provided to override the inertial sensor, this is an inconvenient solution to the problem. SUMMARY. An embodiment of the present invention is a mode of operation in a portable electronic device. The mode of operation is for stabilizing the display of the device with respect to the user's face. The portable electronic device has a camera. The portable electronic device has a display screen. The display mode is switchable between a portrait mode and a landscape mode. The display mode is switchable in response to an inertial sensor. When it is determined that the display mode should be switched in response to movement of the device, a feature of a user of the device is imaged with the camera. When it is determined that the display mode should be switched in response to movement of the device, such as the user's face, is imaged with the camera. If the imaged feature changes orientation with respect to the device by less than a threshold amount, then the switch in display mode is disabled. The display mode remains in its current mode.
